gold.purpose: The mark colour, lifted from the flower in public/logos/yallo-flower.svg. On dark it does everything at 7.07:1; on light it is decorative only at 1.69:1 and must never carry text or state.

gold-deep.purpose: The light-theme accent for anything at large size or acting as a boundary: the italic emphasis inside an H1, oversized numerals, underlines, focus rings. 3.12:1 — clears AA-large and 1.4.11, never small text.

gold-ink.purpose: The light-theme accent for anything small. Every 11px mono eyebrow uses this at 4.69:1. The token exists because the prototype set eyebrows in Struck Gold and shipped a real 3.12:1 AA failure.

gold-wash.purpose: The only tinted ground in the system, for the two commitment badges.

paper.purpose: The default ground. Warm grey-beige, the colour of uncoated stock. Pure white appears nowhere in the light theme.

paper-2.purpose: The lighter alternate ground. Adjacent sections step between the three papers so blocks read as separate sheets without borders.

paper-3.purpose: The darker alternate ground, and the worst case for every light-theme contrast calculation.

ink.purpose: All body copy and headings on light, at 13.69:1.

ink-2.purpose: Section ledes and secondary copy, at 8.42:1.

ink-3.purpose: Captions and meta, at 4.94:1. Raised from the prototype's #63656c, which missed 4.5:1 against Kraft.

rule.purpose: The decorative divider. Hairline rules do the work borders would do elsewhere.

rule-strong.purpose: The contrast-grade border at 3.11:1, for any control whose only boundary is a rule. Required by 1.4.11.

dk.purpose: The dark-theme ground. Charcoal with a whisper of blue, never navy.

dk-2.purpose: The second dark ground, one step up.

dk-3.purpose: The third dark ground, for cards sitting on Appendix Two.

dk-txt-3.purpose: Captions and meta on dark, at 5.40:1.

dk-line.purpose: The decorative divider on dark grounds.

dk-line-strong.purpose: The contrast-grade border on dark, at 3.24:1.

signal-mark.purpose: Scarcity, criticality, hard to fill. Graphical grade at 3:1 or better: fills, dots, bars, strokes. Never a label.

signal-text.purpose: The label grade for scarcity, at 4.5:1 or better on light.

signal-mark-dark.purpose: The scarcity mark grade tuned for near-black.

signal-text-dark.purpose: The scarcity label grade tuned for near-black.

info-mark.purpose: Data series, in-region availability, neutral status. Graphical grade only.

info-text.purpose: The label grade for data series and status, on light.

info-mark-dark.purpose: The data-series mark grade tuned for near-black.

info-text-dark.purpose: The data-series label grade tuned for near-black.

positive-mark.purpose: Renewal rate, filled seats, met milestones. Graphical grade only.

positive-text.purpose: The label grade for renewal and completion, on light.

positive-mark-dark.purpose: The renewal mark grade tuned for near-black.

positive-text-dark.purpose: The renewal label grade tuned for near-black.

category-mark.purpose: An optional fourth data series where three do not suffice. Graphical grade only.

category-text.purpose: The label grade for the fourth series, on light.

category-mark-dark.purpose: The fourth-series mark grade tuned for near-black.

category-text-dark.purpose: The fourth-series label grade tuned for near-black.

display.purpose: The H1, once per page. Capped at 21ch so it breaks into four lines and never runs as a banner. One phrase carries italic 600 in Struck Gold.

lede.purpose: The hero paragraph, in Ink Two, capped at 52ch.

body.purpose: Section ledes and body copy, in Ink Two. 46ch for section ledes, 66ch for article prose.

numeral.purpose: Published metric values, in the display serif.

label.purpose: Eyebrows: uppercase mono in Marker Ink, always preceded by a 5px gold dot. The most repeated element in the system.

data.purpose: Measured values, reference numbers, source lines, timestamps, and the ghost numerals on step cards.

shadows.name: lift
shadows.purpose: The only shadow in the system, declared as --lift in globals.css Layer 1 and referenced exactly once: the hero instrument, the one element pretending to be live rather than printed. A second shadow anywhere destroys its meaning.

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: The default easing token. Button lift, underline wipe, panel swap, chip state.

motion.name: ease-measure
motion.purpose: Reveal and count-up easing on data surfaces, where the motion should decelerate as if settling on a reading.

motion.name: lift-duration
motion.purpose: The primary button's translateY(-2px). Observed value, not a token — durations are set inline against var(--ease).

motion.name: wipe-duration
motion.purpose: The nav underline wipe and the secondary button's gap shift. Observed value, not a token.

motion.name: state-duration
motion.purpose: Card border and ground transitions, the most common state duration in the build. Observed value, not a token.

motion.name: scan-duration
motion.purpose: The hero instrument's sweep, the slowest motion in the system. Gated on prefers-reduced-motion, under which it does not run at all.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The only button on a surface. Gold ground, petal bottom-left, lifts on hover with no shadow.

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: Text with a Struck Gold underline. No box, no ground — it must never compete with the primary.
components.html: See how the screen works

components.name: Dark Button
components.description: Ink ground, Loose Leaf text. Used only where a gold button would be the third gold element in one view.

components.name: Eyebrow
components.description: Section label. Marker Ink at 11px with a 5px gold dot. The most repeated element in the system, and the reason the --gold-ink token exists.

components.name: Card
components.description: Petal at 56px bottom-left, one tonal step from its ground, hairline border. Hover lifts the border and steps the ground; it never adds elevation.
components.html:
Test and quality

The seats cut first and missed most.

components.name: Inverted Card
components.description: The distinguished member of a pair — the gated Blueprint against the open Atlas. It takes the opposite petal corner (top-right) so the difference reads in silhouette before any label does. The corner flip is not an inverted ground: a page has only two inversions to spend.
components.html:
Gated

Programme Staffing Blueprint

Role by role, phase by phase.

components.name: Chip
components.description: Non-interactive label, mono at 12px, petal at 12px. Used for role names and 'right for' lists. Where a chip is actually a control it takes a Boundary border and a gold left edge when selected — never a gold fill, which would collide with the primary button.

components.name: Input Field
components.description: The border is the control boundary, so it takes the contrast-grade Boundary rather than the decorative hairline. Focus shifts the border to Struck Gold and adds an outline; the ground does not change.

components.name: Navigation
components.description: Sticky, Dossier Paper at 94% with the one permitted backdrop blur — a sticky bar over scrolling content needs it to stay legible. Five outward-facing labels with a gold underline that wipes in left-to-right, one quiet Jobs punchout, one button. No per-item colour, no imagery in panels.
components.html: Yallo TalentSpecialismsIndustriesHow we workEvidenceIntelligenceJobs ↗Start a brief →

components.name: Metric with petal fill
components.description: Oversized serif numeral, mono label, definition beneath, and a gold petal whose fill advances a quarter, a half, three-quarters, full across the row of four — so the row reads as a sequence rather than four equal facts. Every metric renders a definition and no source line.
components.html:
80%
Contracts renewed
Placed contractors extended at least once.

components.name: Step card with ghost numeral
components.description: Carried forward from the incumbent build, whose execution of this pattern was stronger than the prototype's derivative of it: icon tile, inline hour badge, and an oversized ghost numeral bled off the bottom-right. The glass, orbs and backdrop blur that surrounded it were not carried.

components.name: Scarcity flag (functional colour)
components.description: The only sanctioned use of a functional colour: a mark-grade dot beside a text-grade label, so meaning never rests on hue alone. Reaching for the mark grade to set the label is the single easiest way to break AA in this system.

narrative.overview:
The product Yallo actually delivers is a document: three names, screening notes, and the reasons seventeen other people were rejected. The site is built as that artefact. Paper-stock grounds instead of white. A serif that belongs to prospectuses and annual reports, not to software. Monospace reserved for the things a dossier sets in monospace — reference numbers, timestamps, source lines, measured values. Gold appears the way an assessor's marker appears on a page someone has actually worked through: sparingly, and only where a judgement was made.

This is chosen against the category, not in ignorance of it. Every benchmarked competitor scores 2 or 3 on visual distinctiveness, and they converge on the same look: photographic hero, rounded cards, blue-to-violet gradient, sans-serif throughout. There is no incumbent to beat here, only a default to refuse. A recruitment site that reads as a printed, annotated document is unclaimed ground, and it happens to be the most honest possible expression of a firm whose entire pitch is we read these people properly before you did.

The register is confident and quiet. Density is editorial: generous measure, hairline rules doing the work borders would do elsewhere, and long uninterrupted runs of type rather than a grid of equal tiles. The one place the system breaks its own stillness is the hero, where a drawn instrument shows a shortlist mid-assembly — because the claim is speed, and speed has to be visible somewhere. Explicitly rejected: stock photography of any kind, glassmorphism and blurred orbs (the incumbent build's register, now anti-reference), per-sector colour coding, and gradient text.
keyCharacteristics: Paper grounds, never pure white; ink, never pure black
One accent, gold, on every page — and nothing else decorative
Serif display over sans body over mono data: three faces, strictly divided by job
The quarter-round petal: three square corners, one radius, taken from the mark
Flat by tonal layering and hairline rules; exactly one lifted element in the whole system
Both themes are first-class and independently AA; neither is an inversion of the other

rules.name: The One Marker Rule
rules.body: Gold is the only colour used decoratively anywhere in the system, and it appears on every page. If a surface needs a second decorative colour, the surface is wrong.

rules.name: The Load-Bearing Colour Rule
rules.body: A functional colour may appear only where hue carries information a reader needs. Never in navigation, buttons, headings or backgrounds. At most three functional colours in any single view. Every one carries an equivalent label or icon, so meaning never depends on hue alone.

rules.name: The Grade Rule
rules.body: Small text takes the -text grade; fills, dots, bars and strokes take the -mark grade. Reaching for a -mark value to set a label is the single easiest way to break AA in this system, and scripts/check-contrast.mjs exists to catch it.

rules.name: The Two Band Rule
rules.body: Within either theme, evidence and data surfaces may invert to the opposite ground. Inversion signals content type, never decoration, and no page carries more than two inverted bands.

rules.name: The Three Jobs Rule
rules.body: Serif for what the page asserts. Sans for what the reader reads. Mono for what was measured. A number that was counted is mono; a number in a sentence is not.

rules.name: The Measure Rule
rules.body: No line of body copy exceeds 66ch, and no headline exceeds 23ch. Both are set as max-width in ch units on the element, not left to the container.

rules.name: The One Lift Rule
rules.body: If a second element in this system acquires a shadow, the first one stops meaning anything. Hover states change ground, border or transform — never elevation.

dos: Do set every 11px mono eyebrow in --gold-ink (#7b5d13), never --gold-deep.
Do step the ground between adjacent sections (paper → paper-2 → paper-warm) so blocks separate tonally without borders.
Do give every functional colour a label or icon alongside it, and run node scripts/check-contrast.mjs before committing any colour change.
Do cap headlines at 23ch and body at 66ch as max-width in ch on the element itself.
Do put the petal radius on exactly one corner, bottom-left by default, top-right on inverted cards.
Do server-render real values and animate from zero only after hydration, and only when motion is permitted.
Do keep both themes independently AA. A change that fixes light and breaks dark is not a fix.
donts: Don't use --gold for text or state on any light ground — it is 1.69:1 and decorative only.
Don't add a second shadow anywhere. Hover changes ground, border or transform.
Don't introduce glass, backdrop blur (outside the sticky nav), blurred orbs, or gradient text. These are the incumbent register and are anti-reference.
Don't use stock photography, invented headshots, or any remote image host.
Don't colour-code by sector, platform or discipline. One accent, always.
Don't put more than two inverted bands on one page, or invert a band for variety rather than to signal content type.
Don't set a counted number in Inter or a sentence's number in mono.
Don't apply border-radius for softness. It is the petal, or it is square.
